subject: Creativity
title: The Three Networks of Creativity
description: Learn The Three Networks of Creativity in one minute.

hook.text: Creativity isn't one brain region. It's three networks that must cooperate like a jazz trio.

buildup.text: The Default Mode Network generates ideas. The Executive Control Network evaluates them.

discovery.text: The Salience Network decides which ideas are worth pursuing — it's the brain's creative editor.

twist.text: Highly creative people show stronger connections between all three — they generate AND filter simultaneously.

climax.text: Less creative thinkers alternate between networks. Creative thinkers run them in parallel.

punchline.text: Creativity isn't wild thinking. It's coordinated thinking.

quiz.question: What does the Salience Network do in the creative process?
options: Decides which ideas are worth pursuing

details.summary: Creative thinking involves three brain networks working together: the default mode network generates ideas, the executive control network evaluates them, and the salience network switches between the two. Highly creative people show stronger connectivity between all three networks.
details.whyItMatters: The three-network model transforms creativity from a mysterious gift into a measurable brain process. It shows that creativity requires not just idea generation but the ability to switch between generating and evaluating modes.
takeaways: Three brain networks collaborate during creative thinking
The salience network acts as a switch between generation and evaluation
Creative people show stronger connectivity between all three networks

faq.question: Can you train these networks?
faq.answer: Practice that exercises switching between idea generation and evaluation strengthens the connectivity between networks. Creative activities that require both brainstorming and refinement, like writing, composing, or design, exercise all three networks and their interactions.

faq.question: Why do some people seem naturally more creative?
faq.answer: Brain imaging shows that highly creative individuals have stronger white matter connections between the three creativity networks. This structural difference may be partly genetic, but creative practice demonstrably strengthens these connections over time.
